claims: `reviewed` may be unreachable, which inverts the change's purpose — `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:766`: `classifyCodeRabbitReviewSignal` reaches `reviewed` only when `isCurrentReviewSignal` is true, and gh's `PullRequestReview` JSON has no commit field, in which case `reviewCommitOid` returns `null` for every real review and the comparison is always false

Consequence if it holds: a genuine exact-head CodeRabbit run classifies `stale`, `fallbackAction` stays `request_review_once_for_head_after_optional_check`, and babysit posts `@coderabbitai review` at closeout on every PR — one wasted round per PR, contradicting the ADR's spend argument at `docs/adr/0066-...md:213-218`
No test uses a recorded gh payload — every fixture in `pr-ready-state.test.mjs` hand-adds a commit field

A clean CodeRabbit run has no `**Run ID**` review and will be re-requested — `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:762`: the loop only inspects `reviews` and requires `/\*\*Run ID\*\*:\s*`…`/`, but the recorded clean completion is a top-level walkthrough comment with no Run ID and no review record, so the signal is `missing`/`stale` and babysit posts a redundant request
The change pushes `pr-ready-state-core.mjs` past the file-size cap — `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:750-790`; raw is now over the 1,000-line hard cap and the file is not on the exempt table

The authority doc orders the closeout after the final pair; the three docs that defer to it say before — `docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:399`; read literally, the authority doc lets an agent all-clear on projections taken before the request went out

Canonical JSON example missing the new fields — `docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:276-306`: the example's `gates` block omits `codeRabbitReviewSignal`, so a consumer reading the example as the shape contract misses the field

Marker comments are accepted from any author — `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:772-786`: the `issueComments` loop checks only the body, not the author or association, so on a public PR anyone can post `@coderabbitai review` plus the marker, flipping the state to `requested` and suppressing the legitimate closeout

Related, same lines: a human typing the bare `@coderabbitai review` resume command named in `.coderabbit.yaml:64` carries no marker, so it's invisible here and babysit will post a second request on top of it

"Idempotent" overstates the mechanism — `babysit-pr/SKILL.md:311` (both copies), `ship/SKILL.md:214`: GitHub has no conditional-create for issue comments, so check-then-post is best-effort duplicate suppression, not idempotency
A residual TOCTOU window exists between re-resolving the head and posting (`babysit-pr/SKILL.md:300-301`)
The rewritten config test is narrower than the old range check
Coverage gap: the second-model side channel was not used because `gh` is disabled
`node scripts/coderabbit-config.test.mjs` could not run — `js-yaml` is not installed in this checkout, so the `.coderabbit.yaml` ↔ `EXPECTED_CONFIG` pin is unverified by execution

Every CodeRabbit fixture in `pr-ready-state.test.mjs` and `pr-feedback-state.test.mjs` is hand-authored, so the green suite says the classifier does what its author intended, not that it matches GitHub or CodeRabbit

1.why: `strings` on gh 2.96.0 shows the `pr view --json reviews` GraphQL fragment is `reviews(first:100){nodes{author{login},authorAssociation,submittedAt,body,state,commit{oid},reactionGroups...}}` — `commit.oid` is present, so `reviewCommitOid` resolves and `reviewed` is reachable

2.why: Consequence rests on claim 1, which is false (gh emits `commit{oid}` for reviews), so the exact-head comparison works and no per-PR wasted request follows

3.why: Literally true that pr-ready-state.test.mjs fixtures are hand-written, but it names no defect — and the hand-added `commit:{oid}` matches gh's real review payload shape

4.why: The only CodeRabbit shapes recorded from a real run in this repo (pr-feedback-state.test.mjs:3355-3373, 'shapes observed on PR #1918') show a clean completion as a top-level walkthrough issue comment with no `**Run ID**`; classifyCodeRabbitReviewSignal (core:760-768) only scans `reviews` for that marker, so such a run reads missing/stale and gets a redundant request

5.why: Same concern as known 'Split the growing ready-state core' (core:750); also mis-stated — the watchlist keys the 1,000 hard cap on `rough` (961) not `raw` (1077), so the file reports 'near hard cap'

6.why: Restates the known docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:408 functional-correctness finding: the authority doc's step 8 closeout after step 5's pair vs operating-card/ship/babysit 'before the final pair' lets all-clear rest on pre-request projections

7.why: docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:276-306 canonical example's `gates` block and top-level fields still omit `codeRabbitReviewSignal`, which the same doc (348-355) and the code now emit

8.why: Matches known core:783 / review-signals:226 'Trust only authorized closeout requests' — the issueComments loop checks only body text, no author or association

9.why: isCodeRabbitFinalHeadReviewRequestBody requires the marker, so a human's bare `@coderabbitai review` (the resume command named at .coderabbit.yaml:64-65) never yields `requested`, unlike classifyCodexReviewSignal which accepts bare `@codex review`; the agent then posts a second request

10.why: Verified the wording at babysit-pr/SKILL.md:311 and ship/SKILL.md:214, but this is a terminology preference about 'idempotent' with no behavioral defect

11.why: SKILL.md:300-301 does say re-resolve then post; the claim states an inherent race with no concrete failure or consequence
